paper.title: Polynomial chaos to efficiently compute the annual energy production in wind farm layout optimization
paper.authors: Andres Santiago Padron, Jared Thomas, Andrew P. J. Stanley, Juan J. Alonso and Andrew Ning

paper_linked_public_data.contents: Grid, Amalia, Optimized and Random 60-turbine layouts plus 72 five-degree wind-direction probabilities

public_source.use: read-only semantic evidence; no source copied
confirmed_elements: constant-Cp/Ct NREL-5MW abstraction and FLORIS parameters
OpenMDAO, DAKOTA, rectangle and SNOPT lifecycle
public_source.target_gap: repository predates the 2019 two-uncertainty study and its executable examples hard-code one uncertainty and ten points

licensed_source_lineage.use: continuous three-zone FLORIS equations and parameter defaults

paper_problem.wind_direction: five-degree measured bins, linearly interpolated and represented by 50 equal-width histogram bins for custom polynomials
paper_problem.wind_speed: Weibull shape 1.8 and scale 12.55 m/s truncated and renormalized to 3-25 m/s
paper_problem.boundary: 14-edge convex hull of Princess Amalia layout

paper_method.basis: custom distribution-orthogonal polynomials with total-order truncation
paper_method.order_selection: ten-fold cross-validation from total order one through candidate maximum
paper_method.gradient: differentiate the responses and reuse the regression linear system to obtain mean gradients
paper_method.optimization: SNOPT sequential quadratic programming through OpenMDAO and pyOptSparse

missing_information: exact two-variable Latin-hypercube and 200000-sample Monte-Carlo arrays
final two-variable DAKOTA input and output files and selected polynomial orders
SNOPT binary, license, version, histories and complete stopping state
exact optimized layouts, random streams and all 120 trajectories
exact target FLORISSE revision and compiled dependency environment
nonzero spline-shift value if one was used
paper_source_conflicts: The paper truncates wind speed to 3-25 m/s while the older public driver uses 0-30 m/s.
The paper reports function precision tolerance 1e-4 while the older source driver requests SNOPT major optimality tolerance 2e-6.
The older public repository implements one uncertain variable at a time and cannot be labelled the final two-variable program.
completion_decisions: Use paper two-variable independence, 3-25 m/s truncation and exact coarse/fine sample counts.
Use deterministic seed-indexed centered Latin hypercubes and disclose that original arrays are absent.
Generate direction- and speed-specific orthogonal polynomial recurrences numerically, select order deterministically with ten folds and use a disclosed small Cholesky ridge.
Translate the continuous three-zone FLORIS value equations independently from Apache-2.0 PlantEnergy lineage and use fixed-width forward automatic differentiation.
Use author-driver constant Cp/Ct, generator efficiency and 5 MW cap; set the unreported spline shift to zero.
Use open NLopt SLSQP in place of proprietary SNOPT and preserve paper constraints, 1000-evaluation limit and source/paper tolerance provenance.
Implement 200000-sample Monte Carlo as evaluation-only reference and do not use it as an optimizer.
Treat paper table values as external anchors rather than numeric acceptance targets.

hpc_contract.persistent_team: one persistent all-core executor per evaluation or optimization
hpc_contract.parallel_axis: independent wind-state wake and derivative evaluations
hpc_contract.gradient_kernel: 120 coordinates in fixed eight-lane forward-AD blocks
hpc_contract.determinism: indexed state writes and ordered regression/AEP reductions give identical one- and all-core scientific receipts
hpc_contract.nonparallel_work: cross-validation, small dense linear algebra, constraints and SLSQP control remain deterministic serial orchestration
hpc_contract.h6_workload: 630-state PC-R fine AEP plus 120-coordinate gradient, repeated three times at one worker and every available Waffle core

claim_boundary: Source-backed flexible academic reproduction of the PC-R method, paper-native two-uncertainty 60-turbine problem and optimization protocol. It is not the author DAKOTA, SNOPT or target FLORISSE execution, original random-state or trajectory replay, or numerical table and timing replay.
